INKLET GUIDES

Draw or type
your PDF signature?

A signature can start with your handwriting or with your name on a keyboard. Here’s how the two options work in Inklet, and how to choose a style that fits your document.

Draw a handwritten signature

The Draw option lets you write directly in the signature panel. Use a mouse on your computer, a trackpad on your laptop, or your finger on a phone or tablet. Your strokes become an image that you can place on the PDF.

This is useful when you want the mark to resemble your usual handwriting. Leave a little space around your strokes, use one comfortable movement, and start again if it feels cramped. You don’t need to fill the entire drawing area: Inklet trims the empty space around your mark.

Type a signature from your name

The Type option turns your entered name into a styled signature image. It can be easier than drawing with a mouse, particularly when using a small trackpad or when a clean, readable name suits the form.

Choose from three styles: Handwritten for a casual script, Classic for a traditional italic serif, or Elegant for a more decorative serif. Review the preview before adding it to your PDF. Your name is rendered as an image, rather than an editable PDF text field.

Choose your ink colour and size

Both methods support green, black, and blue ink. Follow any instructions on the form or from its recipient when choosing a colour. You can change the colour in the signature panel before placing the signature.

After selecting That’s my signature, use the size slider to fit it to the available space. Drag the signature onto the intended line and check that it doesn’t cover other information. Inklet supports one signature placement in the document at a time.

What does a PDF signature image do?

Inklet adds the visible image of your drawn or typed name to a PDF page. You can then download the signed copy and share it using your usual method. Your working PDF stays in your browser during the process.

A visible signature image doesn’t verify who signed the document. Inklet doesn’t create a certificate-based digital signature or a record of signing events. If your recipient requires identity checks, a signing certificate, or an audit trail, this tool doesn’t provide those features. Ask the recipient which process they need.

Try both before choosing

Open the free PDF signature tool and select Try a sample document. Create a drawn signature, then remove it and try a typed one. You can download the sample to see how your choice looks in a finished PDF.

For the complete process from choosing your file to saving the result, follow our step-by-step guide to signing a PDF for free.
